units: USD, nominal, pre-tax, per $100,000 of annual contract rent
disclaimer: Not an appraisal and not a valuation. Contract rent, exact expiry, escalations, basis and debt are unknown. Every dollar figure scales linearly with the owner's actual rent; the percentage breakevens are directly reusable.
comparison_basis: Holding and selling run through the same cash-flow engine with the same escalation, reinvestment rate and exit cap. The sale pays transaction costs and the replacement is bought at the verified net-lease market yield. This is a like-for-like comparison; an earlier version of this script compared a growing asset to a non-growing yield, which is recorded as irregularity F02.

netlease_cash_yield_pct.label: Initial weighted average cash yield on net-lease acquisitions, Q3 2026

netlease_walt_years.label: Reference net-lease portfolio weighted average remaining lease term

county_pop_2025.label: LA County population 2025, CA DOF P-2A

county_pop_2040.label: LA County population 2040, CA DOF P-2A

city_dtt_pct.label: City of LA RPTT base rate

hazard_derivation: annual p = 1 - (1 - p30)^(1/30) from the USGS 30-year Los Angeles-region probabilities (S18).

rent_normaliser.why: Contract rent is unknown (metric L02). Every result is per $100,000 of rent so the owner can scale linearly to their actual rent.

going_in_cap_pct.why: The asset's own cap rate is unpublished (M11). Set equal to the verified Q3 2026 net-lease acquisition cash yield (S17) as the neutral central case. This single number is the one the owner must replace with an appraisal.

expiry_year.why: Midpoint of the 2030-2035 window the brief supplies. The exact date is unverified (L01).

horizon_year.why: Covers the remaining term plus a full renewal cycle.

escalation_pct.why: Typical flat net-lease escalation. The lease was not read (L03).

terminal_cap_pct.why: No cap-rate change assumed over the horizon.

renew_prob.why: No official source exists. Balances a live closure programme (R02) against a site the brand occupies.

downtime_months_if_vacated.why: A drive-through site can only be re-let to entitlement-compatible uses.

relet_cost_pct_of_year_rent.why: Leasing commission plus tenant improvements on a small-format asset.

insurance_recovery_pct.why: Coverage after deductible and limits. The actual policy is unknown (H11, H12).

fire_annual_prob_pct.why: LABELLED ASSUMPTION, NOT OFFICIAL. CAL FIRE publishes hazard zones and loss history (S19, S20) but no parcel annual burn probability. Set low because the parcel is urban; flagged on flag.html.

rate_shock_annual_prob_pct.why: Labelled assumption for a +150bp permanent cap-rate widening.

uplift_at_renewal_pct.why: Central case assumes renewal at the escalated contract rent, i.e. no reset. The breakeven uplift is solved for separately.

scenarios.label: Bear
scenarios.narrative: Wage and insurance costs keep compressing franchisee margin; cap rates widen as the 10-year holds near 4.9%; the tenant extracts a concession or leaves.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.narrative: The verified benchmark holds, rent escalates at 2%, the tenant renews, exit cap unchanged.

scenarios.label: Bull
scenarios.narrative: Rates ease, net-lease demand for drive-through sites strengthens, and the tenant renews early to protect the location.

breakevens.breakeven_note: The numeric threshold differs from the closed form Y*(1-s) because the engine also applies an expected non-renewal loss at the expiry year, which a pure income-capitalisation formula omits.

strategies.name: Negotiate an extension at a market reset, then sell into a 1031 if the price clears the trigger
strategies.detail: Use the tenant's own incentive to stay - a drive-through site inside central LA - to convert a 2030-2035 expiry into a longer term at a rent reset. A longer weighted average lease term is worth more per dollar of rent than the same rent with a near-term rollover, so this improves the hold case and the sale price at the same time.
pros: Attacks the only variable the owner controls: rent and term.
Selling with a fresh ten-year term removes the rollover discount a buyer would otherwise apply.
Keeps the section 1031 route open and defers the tax decision until a replacement exists.
cons: Depends on tenant cooperation, and the tenant is in a closure programme.
An extension does not reduce concentration risk - it only makes the asset more sellable.
Time cost: negotiation, marketing and a 1031 identification is a multi-quarter project.

strategies.name: Sell now into a section 1031 exchange
strategies.detail: Exit at the going-in cap rate, pay brokerage plus county and city transfer tax, and redeploy into two or more net-lease assets or a diversified vehicle, deferring the gain under section 1031.
pros: Removes the single-asset earthquake, wildfire and insurance tail in one transaction.
Converts one illiquid parcel into a diversified, re-priceable position.
Locks in today's cap-rate environment instead of betting it holds to 2032.
cons: Crystallises disposition cost including 0.45% city and 0.11% county transfer tax, and Measure ULA above the indexed threshold.
Requires an identified replacement inside the exchange window; a failed exchange is worse than not selling.
Gives up the Prop 13 assessed-value cap, which is real while held and resets on sale.

strategies.name: Hold to expiry and renew at market
strategies.detail: Do nothing now; negotiate at or before expiry; keep the asset and the lease.
pros: Preserves the Prop 13 cap, which a sale resets.
No transaction cost, no exchange execution risk, no forced timeline.
Retains full optionality until the expiry window opens.
cons: Leaves the decision to a negotiation conducted under time pressure.
Carries the full single-asset hazard exposure for another six to fourteen years.
If the closure programme reaches this unit, the owner holds a vacant drive-through.

strategies.name: Renew long-term and hold as a permanent income asset
strategies.detail: Extend for the longest term available and treat the asset as a permanent income stream.
pros: Maximum contractual certainty of cash flow if the tenant performs.
Best tax profile: no recognition event and the Prop 13 cap continues.
cons: Maximises concentration in a shrinking county, a contracting sector and one credit.
A long lease also blights redevelopment of the land.
Scores worst against the owner's stated requirement to keep risk manageable.

decision.note: Judgement scores on a verified fact base, not measurements. Weights are published so the owner can re-weight and watch the ranking move.

triggers.trigger: An appraisal or broker opinion implies a going-in cap rate below the solved breakeven.
triggers.action: The asset is priced tight relative to what you could buy. Selling wins on arithmetic.

triggers.trigger: An appraisal or broker opinion implies a going-in cap rate above the solved breakeven.
triggers.action: Holding wins on arithmetic. Do not sell to buy a lower yield.

triggers.trigger: A replacement property is identified at or above the required replacement yield.
triggers.action: Execute the exchange. This is the only condition under which selling is a pure upgrade.

triggers.trigger: The tenant will sign an extension at a rent reset.
triggers.reading: uplift required to change the answer is solved in the model
triggers.action: Sign, then sell with the longer term. Best combined outcome for wealth and risk.

triggers.trigger: Insurance cost rises enough to cut net operating income, or a carrier declines the risk.
triggers.action: Sell. Uninsurable or uneconomic cover is the clearest sell signal in this asset class.

triggers.trigger: The option notice date is less than twelve months away.
triggers.action: Stop analysing and start the process. Time becomes the binding constraint, not price.

triggers.trigger: Tenant same-store sales turn positive and the restaurant count stabilises for two consecutive quarters.
triggers.reading: Q3 FY2026: system SSS -1.1%; 2,115 units vs 2,168
triggers.action: Tenant risk is falling; the hold case strengthens and an extension gets easier.
Liquidity overrides optimisation. Sell, accept the cost, and pre-plan the exchange.

triggers.trigger: A parcel-level hazard or insurance finding changes the loss distribution.
triggers.reading: FHSZ, flood zone, seismic screening and earthquake cover all unverified (H08-H12)
triggers.action: Re-run the model with the verified hazard inputs before committing either way.
